topic: Mindful movement program for older breast cancer survivors: a pilot study

sources.title: Mindful movement program for older breast cancer survivors: a pilot study
sources.authors: Crane-Okada R, Kiger H, Sugerman F, Uman GC, Shapiro SL, Wyman-McGinty W, Anderson NL.

findings.finding: Combining mindfulness with movement is a beneficial approach for older survivors to improve their well-being.
findings.quote: The combination of self-directed movement and mindfulness, as tested here, may be a valuable tool for promoting health and well-being in older long-term survivors of breast cancer.

findings.finding: Participants who engaged in a structured movement program reported decreased fear of recurrence and increased mindfulness.
findings.quote: After intervention, EG participants showed improved QOL via decreased fear of recurrence and increased mindfulness attitude.

principle: Integrating mindfulness with self-directed movement can improve quality of life and reduce fear of recurrence in older cancer survivors.
for_the_teacher: Incorporate mindfulness practices, such as focused breathing or stillness, alongside movement sequences.
Encourage learners to engage in self-directed movement to foster a sense of autonomy and well-being.
Provide tools or prompts for learners to track their home practice to support consistency.
when_it_does_not_apply: The study focused specifically on female breast cancer survivors aged 50 and older.
